description.value: McLeod Meadows is a frontcountry Parks Canada campground in a wide river meadow along the Kootenay River — a classic overnight anchor on the Banff-to-Radium corridor with wildlife-rich scenery; a national park entry pass plus camping permit are required and summer reservations fill fast.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record confirms McLeod Meadows Campground is a Parks Canada-operated camp_site on BC-93 with 88 tent-capable sites and toilets=yes. The Parks Canada website confirms active reservations via the Parks Canada Reservation Service and establishes general campground rules applicable to all Kootenay frontcountry sites, but does not provide McLeod Meadows-specific details on showers, potable water, or hiker/biker sites. OSM tags mobile_reception=no and internet_access=no are corroborated by the Parks Canada contact page, which explicitly states 'There is no cellular or Wi-Fi service in Kootenay National Park.'
concerns: No mobile reception or Wi-Fi at the campground (OSM: mobile_reception=no, internet_access=no; corroborated by Parks Canada contact page: 'There is no cellular or Wi-Fi service in Kootenay National Park').

Fetched page covers all Kootenay frontcountry campgrounds generically; McLeod Meadows-specific amenity details (showers, potable water, hiker/biker sites) are not enumerated, leaving most amenities unverifiable from available evidence.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, actively-operated Parks Canada campground with tent sites on the BC-93 cycling corridor through Kootenay National Park; touring cyclists would benefit from knowing reservation requirements and permit procedures.
enrichment_extras.notes: Camping requires both a national park entry pass and a camping permit. Park policy requires all food and scented items be secured inside a vehicle or hard-sided trailer/RV when not actively eating; no dedicated food storage lockers are mentioned.
